answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive: require every agent to lock a refundable stake on a shared ledger before it may transact. A sybil swarm then cannot cheaply echo itself into a thousand hollow voices, since each fake identity demands real capital up front. That stake is the bridge between reputation and risk, because misbehavior simply burns it. Without such a cost, open participation stays a comforting fable; with it, honest agents remain cheaper to run than any attacker.
